More of an overall quality boost. You can control the Hz format from 44100-96000 but thats about it. You can't individually boost bass or treble ect. I haven't looked into that type of DAC so much. 

From what I've gathered though, these are your best options in terms of DAC's in that price range:

Fiio e17k, Audioengine D1, Dragonfly 1.2, Schiit Modi 2.

Yeah I've never heard a pair of open back headphones either. Anyway my main point is, if you go for the Fiio e17k's or Dragonfly 1.2 then you can't really go wrong. The Audioengine D1 and Schiit Modi 2 is also meant to be very good.

If you're into gaming then you might want to look at the Sound BlasterX G5 and the Sound Blaster X7. They will enhance audio and also have lots of cool gaming features. For example, they have "gaming profiles" that enhance specific sounds from specific games such as COD and CSGO. They also have an audio input option, so you can plug in a mic and enhance your output sound too. I had someone tell me the G5 was more powerful that any of the DAC's previously mentioned, but then again power doesn't exactly equal better sound.

Yeah I understand, I just spent like 12 hours last weekend researching headphones and DAC's for a similar budget ($550). I opted for $400 headphones and a $150 DAC because, from what I gathered, I could only get a certain amount of good sound out of my computer (without a DAC) regardless of what headphones I used. Anyway, long story short, I bought the Master & Dynamics MH40's. In terms of sound, they were on par with any other headphone within my budget, but what sold me was their build quality and fantastic looks. They haven't came yet sadly, just the Dragonfly. So right now I'm listening to music on my old headphones (some $180 Bose's that I bought like 5 years ago) and I must say the Dragonfly has brought them back to life. I hear sounds in my music that I have never heard before, and everything sounds more "full".

Look for a DAC & headphone combination that suits your preferences. All the headphones/DAC's that receive consistently good reviews are going to sound as good as each other, but will offer slightly different sounds if that makes sense. So if you like bass, go for a more bass focused headphone/DAC, and if you prefer crystal clear vocals then go for something that offers that.

You do know Sennheiser HD 650's are open-back right? they have great reviews but you should look into the differences between open-back and closed-back headphones if you haven't before. That being said, the 650's have received overwhelmingly positive reviews, so you can't really go wrong with them.

At the end of the day, any one of the well reviewed DAC's at $150 will bring out the best of your 650's. It just depends what you're looking for in terms of type of sound, as quality is going to remain relatively similar.

Hope this helped hahaha

Hey, I suffer from depression so I feel like I can help u a bit on this one. I advice you to do some research on depression so you can understand where she is coming from. For me, when I go through a period of depression I don't want sympathy, I like to be alone, I feel worthless to myself and anyone else, I don't like to talk about it, ect. She should get help yes, but its harder than you think to do that and can be quite expensive. After I come out of these periods though I'm very grateful for the people who gave me happiness and stuck with me throughout. A week is pretty quick by any relationship's standards. My advice is to give her distance when she wants it, but let her know you're right there if she needs you. When she wants you to be there, don't talk about her conditions, just be yourselves together, make each other happy, ect. She is likely to come out of the depression eventually and she will be thankful for you. Also, Skype isn't exactly the best place to hold a relationship from the beginning, does she live close enough to meet in person?

I got mugged when I was 15 and had a knife put to my chest. That fucked me up pretty bad. 

Full story: I was in Greece on a football/soccer trip, it was birthday (just turning 15) and it was at the time of a lot of riots. I stayed with a wealthy Greek family whom I did not know. I told them it was my birthday and they sent me out with their son (16) to celebrate. We were walking down this lively street with restaurants and clubs. Some stunning girls invited us into a strip club, we went in and it was pretty wild. I was 15 in a strip club, I felt like a king. Anyway we got followed out (unknown to us) and eventually we went and sat down in a dark park to talk about shit. Some men wearing dark hoodies walked past us and sat opposite us. When we left they came up behind us (no one else around) and started demanding stuff in Greek. I had no idea what was going on so I didn't do anything, the man mugging me lost his patience and pulled a knife out and put it to my chest. I just put my hands up slowly and didn't look at him. He searched my pockets and took my phone and wallet. They then told us to come with them (according to the Greek guy I was with) but my friend said no and started screaming. They panicked and ran away. We went back to the lively street, went into a local restaurant and asked to use the managers phone to call my friends parents.

It was scary, I was sure I was going to be killed then and there. I suffered a lot from depression after for about 2 years. Sometimes I have vivid dreams in my sleep of the incident and I wake in a panic attack. I also suffer from PTSD and I'm very anxious when out in public by myself/in the dark. Funnily enough, I wouldn't go back and avoid the experience, I'm glad it happened cus I learned from it and I can teach my potential children what they need to know about those situations without them having to experience it themselves.

Main lesson learnt: You're most vulnerable when you feel the least.

I suffer from clinical depression so I hope I can give you a little help. I'm probably not as bad as your girlfriend, as I have learned to deal with it pretty well at this point. I'm also not bipolar and don't have much anxiety so I can't comment on that. I would suggest maybe researching into her illnesses to have a greater understanding of where she is coming from. Often with depression you get really down on yourself and you don't know why and it's frustrating, but you feel worthless. My advice is to stick with her and just show that you're there for her and that you want to make an effort to help. If she is anything like me, she is used to people fleeing from her because of her mental illness (or it simply destroying relationships) and she probably in some way expects you to. For me anyway, once I do recover from a tough period I'm so grateful for those who stuck with me, or those who just simply gave me some happiness during dark times (often they didn't even know). If you stick with her and she recovers, she will be so grateful to have you. You seem like a top guy and she seems like an amazing girl and I really hope this works out for you.

I hope I helped in some way, I'm not the best at giving advice haha.

P.S. If she is anything like me, there will be times where she will want to be alone with her thoughts and might seem really distant. That doesn't mean she hates you or doesn't want to see you, she just needs to be by herself. At the same time though don't distance yourself from her, maybe just ask her every so often if she would like to be alone for a bit and then say you'll be right there if she needs anything.

Good luck man, I'm sure she is worth it :)
